frequency_question: How often do state supreme courts allow a challenged map to proceed rather than blocking it or missing the window when acting under a compressed pre-election timeline?
membership_rule: Includes state supreme court rulings on emergency applications to stay lower court rulings or approve disputed congressional/legislative maps within 30 days of an electoral deadline. Excluded are federal court actions and routine redistricting cycles without emergency pre-election timing constraints.

coverage_note: 10 named emergency state supreme court map interventions; estimated total population of comparable high-salience compressed-timeline state supreme court map interventions since 2018 is roughly 14.
known_gaps: Omits minor state court dockets where opinions were unrecorded or dismissed on procedural standing without reaching the merits.
validity_reason: The baseline judicial behavior and procedural friction governing emergency election dockets remain stable across a typical federal two-year election cycle up to the next major redistricting cycle.
